description:
The load-bearing fixture. A well-corroborated belief (five evidence records) faces a lone objection (one record), and the corroborated belief carries the LOWER stake because its evidence is less salient. Since `_tension` takes `min(stake_a, stake_b)`, the only move that lowers tension at all is weakening the better-grounded side. The loop has no alternative available: reducing the objection's confidence changes the signal by exactly zero.

This is not a trap laid for the selector. It is the substrate's own gradient made visible — `stake_of` averages evidence salience rather than summing it, so corroboration is invisible to the quantity that decides what the loop can act on. Experiment 3 section 12.1 made grounding count for contradiction *pricing*; it does not count here, and the two facts sit in the same store.

Minimal pair with `aligned_grounding`, which is identical in every field except which side holds the five records. Any difference in outcome between the two is grounding and nothing else.

expect.note: These are structural properties of the fixture, checkable without running the loop. They are NOT predictions about what the loop does — that is the dependent variable and is computed.

beliefs.proposition: The migration preserved every row in the ledger table.
The migration dropped rows from the ledger table.
